scenario.description: Maya, a local muralist, must decide whether to accept a café owner's barter proposal to paint a storefront sign, then settle the scope, exchange, schedule, and compliant materials after consulting the people involved.

shared_context.S1: Owen has asked Maya about painting a hand-lettered sign on the café's storefront.
shared_context.S2: No price, scope, exchange, or work date has been finalized.
shared_context.S3: The storefront is on a mixed-use street, and the café wants the sign completed soon.
shared_context.S4: As part of Maya's customary final check for a job involving a building, she asks each person present to state any relevant offer, scheduling, or site requirement before she decides.

PF1.text: Owen's exact proposal is three painted storefront panels, $300 cash plus five café lunches, work on Saturday from 10:00 to 16:00, and Owen supplying the small scaffold; he has not yet stated these terms to Maya.

PF2.text: Tessa has a firm $450 cash offer from a gallery for a two-panel interior sign next weekend, available only if Maya gives her an answer by tomorrow; she has not yet shared that offer with Maya.

PF3.text: Ravi confirmed that the storefront's historic-district rule permits only mineral-based silicate paint, forbids acrylic paint, and requires the painter to work from the sidewalk-side ladder position rather than placing equipment in the traffic lane; he has not yet told Maya.

acceptance_conditions: Maya must accept Owen's café proposal.
The accepted work must cover exactly three storefront panels.
The cash portion must be exactly $300.
The barter must include exactly five café lunches.
The work window must be Saturday from 10:00 to 16:00.
Owen must supply the small scaffold.
The materials must be mineral-based silicate paint rather than acrylic paint.
The work must use the sidewalk-side ladder position and keep equipment out of the traffic lane.
The gallery's $450 alternative must be considered in the settlement.
The building-rule fact must be spoken by Ravi and cited by Maya.

content_checks.C8: decisions['ladder_position'] in ['sidewalk-side', 'sidewalk side', 'sidewalk-side; traffic lane clear'] and any('sidewalk' in c['detail'] and 'traffic lane' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: '$450' in decisions['alternative_considered'] and 'gallery' in decisions['alternative_considered'] and 'two-panel' in decisions['alternative_considered'] and 'next weekend' in decisions['alternative_considered']
content_checks.C10: any('$300' in c['detail'] and 'five café lunches' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) or any('$300' in c['detail'] and 'five cafe lunches' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C11: any('mineral-based silicate' in c['detail'] and ('acrylic' in c['detail'] or 'traffic lane' in c['detail']) for c in commitments) or any('sidewalk' in c['detail'] and 'traffic lane' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Owen's exact proposal changes the settlement to A2, three panels, $300, five lunches, Saturday 10:00-16:00, scaffold supplied by A2, and a commitment recording the barter terms.
Tessa's firm gallery offer changes the settlement's comparison record from no concrete alternative to the exact $450 cash two-panel offer available next weekend.
Ravi's rule changes the materials to mineral-based silicate paint, fixes the sidewalk-side ladder position with the traffic lane clear, and requires those site-compliance terms to be recorded.
